acknowledgementSource: Existing CommandHandoffControl.request two-second confirmation contract; shared end-to-end by local and remote controls, not a new timeout or retry budget.
result: null means no task or swarm session for this authenticated owner. Otherwise interrupt returns a boolean interrupted and a positive integer pid only on success; background returns a boolean backgrounded; swarm_abort returns a boolean aborted; swarm_agent_stop returns a boolean stopped and the agent status it decided on. Each may include a string reason. swarm_status returns the owner's session resident in that process as GET /api/v4/swarm/status serves it: a boolean active, known true, optional booleans terminated and awaitingContinue, and a list of agent rows. background_activity is never null: it returns the owner's swarms and backgroundCommands lists. storage_rpc_metrics is never null: it returns histograms, one {labels, buckets, counts, sum, count} row per series of the incarnation's tofu_storage_rpc_seconds histogram, labels being the closed kind/operation/outcome catalog and counts cumulative per bucket. task_view returns task, the public task view GET /api/v4/tasks/{id} serves, and workUnit, that task's work-unit block or null; task_abort returns a boolean aborting and the string status it observed; guidance_answer returns a boolean resolved. mcp_reconcile is never null: it returns a boolean scheduled, false once the incarnation is shutting down. Malformed or mismatched results never certify success.
transport: One loopback connection per control request. A network-order u32 byte length precedes one UTF-8 JSON object. There is no automatic retry or detached accepted-work queue.

semantics.authority: A manager-owned execution incarnation publishes a private endpoint and rotating bearer secret in its existing protected process record. Only the authenticated API owner and exact task/round/tool-call identity reach the existing TaskRuntime command control owner. Hints, file existence and a task ID alone grant no authority.
semantics.interrupt: Interrupt targets the currently live process occurrence by its PID stamp. No request remains queued to affect a later command.
semantics.background: The existing command worker alone transfers its pipes and publishes the background handle. Delivery of a request is never reported as successful handoff.
semantics.swarm: A swarm session lives in the process that runs its spawning conversation. swarm_abort and swarm_status address it by swarm key or task alias, swarm_agent_stop by its run ID (taskId) and params.agent_id; they apply the existing in-process abort_swarm, resident_swarm_status and stop_swarm_agent owners. The local process answers first; only an absent session is asked of the execution incarnation. The status route reads the durable row only after neither process holds the session, so a live session never reads as an unknown non-terminal row; an unconfirmed incarnation is unavailable, never unknown.
semantics.production: A production work unit (slide deck, film, report, research job) lives in the TaskRuntime of the process that started it: Chat tools start them in the execution incarnation, HTTP starters in the API. task_view and task_abort address one by task ID and apply the existing owner-scoped TaskRuntime read and abort_owned; Chat tasks are never addressed by these methods and keep their durable paths. guidance_answer addresses a pending human gate (an opt-in outline or storyboard review, or an ask_human question) by its guidance ID in taskId with params.response and applies the existing resolve_human_guidance owner, including its durable answer receipt for Chat gates. The local process answers first; only an absent task or gate is asked of the execution incarnation, and an unconfirmed remote answer is unavailable, never not found.
semantics.mcp: An MCP bridge is process-local and Turns call tools through the execution incarnation's. After the API applied an owner's MCP management action (connect, disconnect, remove, per-tool enable/disable) to its own bridge, mcp_reconcile with params.server and params.action (connect, disconnect or tools) queues the same action on the incarnation's owned MCP startup worker, which connects with the owner's current stored row, disconnects, or applies the row's disabled_tools grant without reconnecting. The acknowledgement confirms only the queueing; the connection settles asynchronously and its failures stay in that process's MCP health.
semantics.ownerMethods: An owner method carries an empty taskId and reports the owner's whole process-local view. background_activity lists live swarm sessions and running background commands; the API unions its own view with the execution incarnation's and an unconfirmed remote view is unavailable, never empty. storage_rpc_metrics reports process-wide storage RPC latency, which holds no owner data; only the admin-scoped /metrics route requests it, and it is exported beside, never merged into, the API's own histogram.
semantics.shards: The execution incarnation may run on-demand execution shards (serverctl_pkg/execution_shards.py), each with its own listener known only to the incarnation. The incarnation answers from its own process first, then asks each shard within the request's own deadline: the first non-null answer wins; an unconfirmed shard makes the answer unavailable, never null. background_activity unions every shard's view; mcp_reconcile is repeated on every shard and is scheduled only when every process scheduled it; storage_rpc_metrics reports the incarnation process only.
semantics.failure: Missing or stale execution incarnation, invalid authentication and malformed requests fail closed. Lost responses are unknown and never cause an automatic replay. Existing authoritative tool results resolve user-visible outcome.
semantics.lifecycle: The execution application owns one listener. Closing withdraws admission and joins entered control callbacks before worker shutdown; cancelling a network observer never abandons physical callbacks.
semantics.retention: Only current accepted connections and their callbacks are retained until joined. No durable task state, control ledger or second task registry is created.
